rationale:
bugs_open/283, round 2. Round 1 returned REVISE (4 approve, 5 object) and this submission acts on the objections rather than re-arguing them.

THE DEFECT. A component's element ids are literal text. Two instances on one page claim the same ids, so document.getElementById hands every lookup to the first copy: the second calculator renders, accepts typing, responds to its button, and answers from the FIRST one's inputs. On a consumer-credit site that is a page showing a repayment figure computed from numbers the visitor never entered — a plausible wrong answer, not an error. Measured 2026-08-15: 173 of 240 active components hardcode at least one element id (166 literal-only), 100 bind by getElementById, and one id (btn-calculate) is shared by NINE different calculators, so listing different calculators on one page collides too. The owner ruled that reuse should be a genuine property of the platform.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1, objection by objection.

(1) reuse_agent, HIGH — 'the slot fallback writes the SAME key with a WEAKER guarantee ... reproduces, under a new name, the exact ComponentID landmine this plan's own rationale diagnoses.' Accepted in full. InstanceTokenFromSlot is DELETED. There is now one rule (component function + occurrence on the page) and one derivation (InstanceCounter). The two paths that cannot see the whole page supply occurrence 0 to that same rule rather than deriving a token of their own — a possibly-wrong INPUT to one rule, not a second rule with a second guarantee, and the difference is that a wrong occurrence produces a COLLISION, which DetectInstanceCollisions already reports.

(2) bug_historian, MEDIUM — 'three call sites patched, the mechanism left generic.' Accepted, and the seat was right about the class while wrong about the members, which is the point. It named five files; four of them do not call a RenderTemplate* helper at all. Measured 2026-08-16 across the whole repo: EIGHT non-test files hold FOURTEEN calls. Three bound a token; of the five that did not, four are single-instance by construction (site chrome, <head>, and an offline lint) and one — the section editor, on nobody's list — renders a page-embedded component and bound nothing. My own first census also missed cmd/component-render-check, because it grepped platform/ and internal/ and that file lives in cmd/. That is exactly why the answer here is not a better list: the shared render layer now REPORTS a template that needs a token and was given none, and scripts/pattern-check.py refuses a new render call site that binds neither seam unless it is allow-listed with a measured reason.

(3) prior_art_librarian, MEDIUM — 'you didn't check page_components.data_uuid.' Checked: 1,580 rows, 1,580 populated, 1,580 distinct. Uniqueness is provable rather than derived, so it is the stronger column and it is still the wrong choice, for the reason that decided the whole design — see below.

(4) reuse_agent + constitution, MEDIUM — 'a per-instance value already exists on that exact line' (assemble_from_library.go:277, component_<function>_<idx>). Fair. The new token is that idea with the estate's one rule applied to it, not a second parallel token; the legacy string stays only because ComponentID is load-bearing for five live components and re-pointing it changes their served ids, which is an architecture-scope change and is filed as the follow-up the architecture seat asked for.

(5) guardian, LOW — 'the detector is wired into nothing' and 'no end-to-end test that two instances actually get two different InstanceIDs.' Added: TestRenderLayer_twoInstancesOnOnePageGetDifferentIDs drives the real seam (template with {{.InstanceID}} -> real RenderContext binding -> real RenderTemplate -> detector), and carries a mutation in which the same template is rendered through a path that binds nothing, which must collide.

(6) editquality + guardian, HIGH — 'InstanceTokenFromSlot is undefined; this does not compile.' A submission artefact, and my fault: I added the helper after writing the sketch and never updated it. Every symbol this round names is included in the sketches below.

THE DESIGN DECISION, which is the one thing a reviewer should press on. The token is component FUNCTION + OCCURRENCE (c-mortgages-repayment, then c-mortgages-repayment-2), not position and not data_uuid. Both rejected candidates give provable or near-provable uniqueness WITHIN a page and both fail ACROSS pages: measured, the LMC tool slot sits at position 0 on 7 pages and position 1 on the other 16, and a data_uuid differs per row by construction. Under either, one component answers to different ids on different pages, so every hand-written selector needs per-page knowledge — loanandmortgagecalculator's oracle.py addresses all 170 of its checks by literal CSS id. Function+occurrence is the same on every page for a component that appears once, which is every interactive component on every live page today. The cost is that uniqueness is DERIVED from the page's ordered section list rather than read off a unique column, and that cost is paid by the detector.

Nothing consumes any of this yet: measured 2026-08-16, zero of 243 active component templates reference {{.InstanceID}}, so the change is inert in production and the token shape is still free. The 22 calculator templates are unconverted, so 283 stays OPEN.

plan.summary: Give every render path ONE per-instance identity for component element ids, so a component carrying ids and scripts can appear twice on one page. Round 1 shipped a position-derived token plus a slot-derived fallback with a weaker guarantee under the same key; this round replaces both with a single rule (component function + occurrence on the page), one derivation (InstanceCounter), two named binding seams, a report at the shared render layer for a template that needs a token and was given none, and a pattern-check that refuses a new unbound render call site. No template consumes the value yet, so production behaviour is unchanged.

edits.symbol: InstanceToken, InstanceCounter, InstanceTokensForPage, BindInstanceToken, BindSingleSectionInstanceToken, TemplateNeedsInstanceID, InstanceContentKey
edits.rationale: One rule and one derivation, replacing round 1's two. InstanceTokenFromSlot (the reuse_agent's HIGH objection) is deleted outright rather than renamed, because the defect was not its name — it was a second uniqueness guarantee reachable through the same key.

The reuse_agent's HIGH objection, at its site. This path renders one section and, during a build, the page_components rows may not exist yet, so there is nothing to count against — it supplies occurrence 0 to the canonical rule instead of deriving a token from the slot name.

-		renderCtx.ContentData["InstanceID"] = InstanceTokenFromSlot(instanceSlot)
-	}

+	// and a different SHAPE, so one instance's ids depended on which action last

edits.rationale: THE ACTUAL GAP, and it was on no list — not the council's five, not my three. Both sites render a page-embedded component into page_components.rendered_html and bound nothing at all, so a converted template edited or swapped here would have rendered an empty token and put every instance back on identical ids.
edits.sketch:
@@ applyContentEdit
+	// One section, so the page's other instances are not in scope — occurrence 0
+	// into the canonical rule. Without this {{.InstanceID}} renders "" under
+	// missingkey=zero and every instance takes identical element ids.
+	BindSingleSectionInstanceToken(renderCtx, getStringVal(componentData, "function"))
 	rendered := RenderTemplate(htmlTemplate, renderCtx, logger)

@@ applyComponentSwap
+	BindSingleSectionInstanceToken(renderCtx, comp.Function)
 	rendered := RenderTemplate(comp.HTMLTemplate, renderCtx, logger)

edits.rationale: This path walks the page's components in render order, so it uses the canonical counter. Also removes the hand-rolled map write in favour of the named seam, which is what makes the pattern-check below mechanical.
edits.sketch:
var componentFunctions []string
+	// One counter for the whole page, advanced in render order.
+	instances := NewInstanceCounter()
 	for idx, componentName := range componentNames {
@@
-		if renderCtx.ContentData == nil { renderCtx.ContentData = make(map[string]interface{}) }
-		renderCtx.ContentData["InstanceID"] = InstanceToken(idx)
+		BindInstanceToken(renderCtx, instances.Next(comp.Function))

edits.rationale: The path that actually serves re-rendered pages. Same counter, walked in position order (loadStoredSections orders by position). The counter deliberately does not advance for a CARRIED section, whose stored HTML is reused and contributes no new ids; the consequence is stated at the call site rather than hidden.
edits.sketch:
var cta *rerenderCTAState
+	instances := NewInstanceCounter()
 	for _, s := range stored {
@@
-		rc.ContentData["InstanceID"] = InstanceToken(s.position)
+		// The counter advances only for sections that RESOLVED a component: a carried
+		// section keeps its stored HTML and contributes no new ids, so counting it
+		// would shift every later token for no reason. Consequence, stated: if a
+		// previously-unresolvable component starts resolving, later tokens move and
+		// that re-render is not byte-identical.
+		BindInstanceToken(rc, instances.Next(comp.Function))

edits.rationale: bug_historian's MEDIUM, at the shared layer where every one of the fourteen call sites arrives. It REPORTS and does not substitute: this layer cannot see the page, so any token it invented would either collide (no better than empty) or disagree with the token the page's other paths use for the same instance — which is worse than empty, because the ids would then depend on which action last touched the section. Placed beside, and modelled on, the form_action seeding that already makes a caller-dependent guarantee mechanical here.

The durable half of bug_historian's objection: a census of call sites is what goes stale, and this one went stale twice in one round (the council's list and mine). The check matches the CALL, not the argument's name — an earlier draft required the argument to be spelled htmlTemplate, which is the same staleness one rung down. Same idiom as check_unrepaired_component_write, including the raw-body/stripped-body split, so this is one mechanism rather than a second.
edits.sketch:
+COMPONENT_RENDER_RE = re.compile(r"\bRenderTemplate\w*\s*\(")
+INSTANCE_BIND_SEAM_RE = re.compile(r"(?:BindInstanceToken|BindSingleSectionInstanceToken)\s*\(")
+
+def _binds_instance_token(raw):
+    for line in raw.splitlines():
+        bare = line.lstrip()
+        if bare.startswith("//") or bare.startswith("*"): continue  # prose is not a call
+        if INSTANCE_BIND_SEAM_RE.search(line): return True
+    return False
+
+# Reasons, not exemptions — each a MEASURED claim about the SLOT, not the file.
+INSTANCE_TOKEN_ALLOWED = {
+  "component_library.go": "RenderHeader/RenderFooter/RenderHead render CHROME via ResolveChromeComponent — one per document; this file also hosts the shared reporting seam",
+  "render_site_components_action.go": "site chrome slots, one instance per page by construction",
+  "rerender_pages_actions.go": "renders the <head> template only (:532)",
+  "rendercheck.go": "offline lint: writes its report to doc_notes (:507), never to rendered_html or a served page, and synthesises a marker for every referenced field (:315-350)",
+}
+
+def check_unscoped_component_render(files, ref, findings):
+    for path in files:
+        if not path.endswith(".go") or path.endswith("_test.go"): continue
+        if os.path.basename(path) in INSTANCE_TOKEN_ALLOWED: continue
+        content = file_content(path, ref)
+        if not content: continue
+        if not COMPONENT_RENDER_RE.search(strip_comments(content)): continue  # OFFENCE stripped
+        if _binds_instance_token(content): continue                            # GUARD raw
+        findings.append(("unscoped-component-render", path, ...))

edits.rationale: The guardian's end-to-end test, plus a regression test for each accepted objection. Every clean assertion is paired with a mutation of the same input that must come out dirty, because a detector that reports nothing is indistinguishable from one that is inert.

grounded_in: council round 1, reuse_agent seat (HIGH): 'reproduces, under a new name, the exact ComponentID landmine this plan's own rationale diagnoses: one field name, two different uniqueness guarantees, indistinguishable on any page where only one instance is present.'
council round 1, architecture seat: 'The estate needs one canonical per-instance identity, not three ad hoc derivations sharing a name.'
council round 1, bug_historian seat (MEDIUM): 'three call sites patched, the mechanism left generic' — RenderTemplate still defaults a missing key to empty string.

Measured 2026-08-16, whole repo, `git ls-files '*.go'` minus tests: EIGHT files hold FOURTEEN calls to a RenderTemplate* helper. Five bound no token before this change; four of those five are single-instance by construction (chrome, <head>, offline lint) and one — section_editor_actions.go, two sites — renders a page-embedded component.

Measured 2026-08-16, live DB: SELECT count(*) FROM content_components WHERE html_template LIKE '%InstanceID%' -> 0, against 243 active components. Nothing consumes the token yet, so the shape is still free and the change is inert in production.
Measured 2026-08-15, live DB: the LMC tool slot sits at position 0 on 7 pages and position 1 on the other 16 — so a position-derived token gives one component two different ids across pages.
Measured 2026-08-15, live DB: page_components.data_uuid — 1,580 rows, 1,580 populated, 1,580 distinct. Provably unique per row, and per-row is precisely what makes it differ per page.

Measured 2026-08-15, live DB: 173 of 240 active components hardcode at least one element id (166 literal-only); 100 bind by getElementById; btn-calculate is shared by NINE different calculator components.

scripts/pattern-check.py, check_unscoped_component_render run over every non-test .go file in the repo: 4 findings at HEAD (the four page-embedded renderers), 0 in the working tree. The check was proven able to fail on the motivating case before being trusted.

Mutation-tested, three mutations each killed by the test written for it: counter never advances -> the repeat test and the end-to-end test fail; BindSingleSectionInstanceToken given its own shape -> the agreement test fails with 'c-mortgages-repayment-slot' vs 'c-mortgages-repayment'; TemplateNeedsInstanceID returns false -> its own test fails.
plan.risks:
1. UNIQUENESS IS DERIVED, NOT READ OFF A COLUMN. Two instances get distinct tokens only if the rendering path walked the page's ordered section list. The two single-section paths cannot, and supply occurrence 0; on a page that really does carry two instances rendered one section at a time, both take the same token and collide. That is the accepted cost of choosing selector stability over provable uniqueness, and DetectInstanceCollisions is what pays it. A reviewer who thinks the trade is wrong should say so — data_uuid is the alternative and it is one query change away.
2. THE ENFORCEMENT IS STILL OFF. enforce_instance_scope defaults to false, so a collision is recorded and not refused. It cannot default on: 13 active pages already emit duplicate ids today (generic-text-block resolving its one id through the shared ComponentID), so refusing would fail their next re-render and turn a latent defect into an outage.
3. THE DETECTOR IS A REGEX SCAN, NOT AN HTML PARSE, and the concatenation it checks EXCLUDES chrome — so a collision between a section and the header or footer is invisible to it. A clean result is not a clean page.
4. THE PATTERN-CHECK IS ADVISORY AND FILE-SCOPED. It fires per changed file; a render call site added to an allow-listed file inherits the exemption silently. component_library.go is the one that matters, because it hosts both the chrome renderers and the shared seam.
5. CONVERTING THE TEMPLATES ENDS THE BYTE-IDENTICAL PROPERTY the LMC lane verifies against (b2_verify's verbatim-render check needs rebaselining), and oracle.py's 170 literal-id selectors must move in lockstep. Neither is done in this change: the 22 calculator templates are unconverted and 283 stays OPEN.
6. NOT CHANGED, DELIBERATELY: {{.ComponentID}} still means two different things on two paths. Re-pointing it would change the served ids of five live components, which is architecture-scope; it is the follow-up the architecture seat asked for and is recorded as such rather than smuggled in here.
